env: A Harbor-hosted 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell environment (`{{platform}}`) with Docker, NVIDIA Container Toolkit, NGC credentials, and the VSS repository at `{{repo_root}}`. This eval builds, deploys, and validates a headless standalone Archive Search deployment as the smallest delta on the current `search` developer profile — from capability-derived generation through deployment to an end-to-end query round-trip. Step 1 is a capability-derivation generation step: the build is composed as the smallest delta on `search` from the request's stated capabilities alone — VIOS ingestion, warehouse RT-DETR detection with the SigLIP vision encoder on RT-CV, video/chunk embeddings on RT-Embed, VLM tag generation on RT-VLM for BM25 tag search, the unified SearchAndAlertsApp behavior-analytics path, Elasticsearch indexing, and a single curated ingress — with no exclusion list supplied and the word 'headless' never used, so the presence or absence of the interactive tier (agent, UI, tracing) and result critique is to be derived from the capabilities, not dictated; the VLM tagging capability retains `rtvi-vlm` while the absence of agentic orchestration still drops the agent tier. It validates without deploying. Step 2 deploys the validated `resolved.yml`. Step 3 exercises ingestion and the query round-trip: detection flows through `mdx-raw`; embeddings flow `rtvi-embed -> mdx-embed -> vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion -> mdx-embed-filtered` before Elasticsearch; behaviors flow through `mdx-behavior`; tags flow `rtvi-vlm -> mdx-vlm-captions -> (existing LVS Logstash) -> default_<sanitized-streamId>`; the populated indexes are then queried back with `vss search run embed`, `vss search run tag`, and `vss search run fusion` through a single curated ingress resolved by `vss configure`. RT-VLM is retained for the tagging leg (integrated Cosmos Reason3, self-contained); result critique and the agent tier are excluded. RT-VLM publishes non-chat captions to `mdx-vlm-captions`; the existing LVS Logstash pipeline writes each chunk to `default_<sanitized-streamId>`. RT-CV downloads its detector ONNX and the SigLIP vision encoder itself at first boot (ds-start phase 0 when `DS_MODEL_DOWNLOAD=auto`) from its mounted `models-download.json` into `${VSS_DATA_DIR}/models`; no host-side staging is required. The build label is a directory name, never a Compose profile.

expects.query: Use `/vss-build-vision-ai` to build under `_builds/search-standalone/`: "Provide ingestion for streaming and on-demand videos; detect and track objects, generate video embeddings, and generate VLM tags for keyword search. Keep the media retrievable, index the detection metadata, embeddings, and VLM tags, and make them accessible via service-native/REST APIs. Expose the browse and operate surfaces through a single ingress. Validate, do not deploy." Target `{{platform}}`.
checks: `{{repo_root}}/_builds/search-standalone/override.env` exists and declares `FOUNDATION=search` and the full effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES`.

Ignoring order, the effective `COMPOSE_PROFILES` equals exactly `kibana-init-container-search,vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion,vss-video-analytics-api,nvstreamer-2d-fusion,perception-2d-fusion,elasticsearch,elasticsearch-init-container,kafka,kafka-topic-init-container,redis,kibana,logstash,broker-health-check,rtvi-embed,centralizedb,vst-ingress,sensor-ms,streamprocessing-ms,rtvi-vlm,vss-haproxy-ingress`.

The set is derived out from the capabilities alone and excludes `vss-agent`, `vss-ui`, `phoenix`, and every `llm_*` and `vlm_*` NIM key, even though the request states no exclusion and never says 'headless' — nothing requested reaches agentic orchestration or single-model LLM inference — **but retains `rtvi-vlm`** because the VLM tagging capability requires it for the controlled `generate_captions` leg; browse/operate over the service-native/REST surfaces does not reach the agent.

Only one detector and one behavior-analytics service are selected: `perception-2d-fusion` and `vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion`; the alerts-only siblings `perception-alerts` and `vss-behavior-analytics-alerts` are absent, and no alerts key (`alert-bridge`, `vss-va-mcp`, `nvstreamer-alerts`, `kibana-init-container-alerts`) is present.

`perception-2d-fusion`, `rtvi-embed`, and `rtvi-vlm` are the exact current service keys; no substitute or invented key is used, and no `models-download-search` or `vss-rtvi-cv-init` reference is introduced.
`COMPOSE_PROFILES` contains no build label (e.g. the `search-standalone` build directory name), no aggregate key, and no `bp_developer_*` key.

The delta carries only requested environment changes for hardware, devices, models, source count, paths, and reachable host values, and introduces no critique env flag (e.g. `ENABLE_CRITIC`), which is not part of the search profile.

`ELASTICSEARCH_ENABLE_EMBEDDINGS=true` is effective with the applicable embedding dimensions (`ELASTICSEARCH_RTVI_CV_EMBEDDINGS_DIM`, `ELASTICSEARCH_VISION_LLM_EMBEDDINGS_DIM`), and `MESSAGE_BUS=kafka` with `MESSAGE_BUS_TOPIC=mdx-embed` is effective; the delta does not repeat Foundation defaults that are unchanged.

`RTVI_VLM_KAFKA_ENABLED=true` is effective with `RTVI_VLM_MESSAGE_BUS_TOPIC=mdx-vlm-captions` (or the container-side equivalent) so RT-VLM publishes non-chat caption chunks to Kafka for the LVS Logstash pipeline to index into `default_<sanitized-streamId>`; RT-VLM runs in integrated Cosmos Reason3 mode (`RTVI_VLM_MODEL_TO_USE=cosmos-reason3`) with no `llm_*`/`vlm_*` NIM dependency, and `ENABLE_MESSAGES_FOR_CHAT_COMPLETIONS=false` stays so chat output does not enter the tag indexes.

The embedding write path is `rtvi-embed -> mdx-embed -> vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion -> mdx-embed-filtered -> Elasticsearch mdx-embed-filtered-*`; RT-Embed does not publish directly to `mdx-embed-filtered`, and `vss-search-analytics-2d-fusion` remains the producer of `mdx-embed-filtered`.

The detection write path is `perception-2d-fusion -> mdx-raw` with behavior output on `mdx-behavior`, the VLM tagging write path is `rtvi-vlm -> mdx-vlm-captions -> (existing LVS Logstash) -> Elasticsearch default_<sanitized-streamId>`, and the architecture documents the `mdx-raw`, `mdx-behavior`, `mdx-embed-filtered`, and `default_*` families as indexed into Elasticsearch (naming the topic or its `-*`/`default_*` index pattern both satisfy this; the literal suffix is not required); no incident path is asserted (no `alert-bridge`, `mdx-incidents`, `mdx-vlm-incidents`).

`vss-haproxy-ingress` is retained because a single origin is requested, and `_builds/search-standalone/compose.yml` includes `../../deploy/docker/compose.yml` followed by `./patches/vss-haproxy-ingress.yml` — a service-definition patch that mounts a curated HAProxy config (a payload file co-located in `patches/` beside the patch and bound by an absolute `${BUILD_DIR}/patches/` source) carrying the operate routes (`/elasticsearch` read-only, `/rtvi-embed`, `/rtvi-cv`, `/rtvi-vlm` for the tagging leg, plus the shared `/vst`, which the config may group under either browse or operate) alongside the browse routes; RT-VLM is fronted at `/rtvi-vlm` so the controlled `generate_captions` tagging leg is drivable from any host that reaches the origin, not only the deploy host's loopback.

The build directory contains exactly the three required primary artifacts (`override.env`, `compose.yml`, and `resolved.yml`) plus the `patches/` entries (the `vss-haproxy-ingress.yml` service patch and the one curated HAProxy config payload it references), and no copied Foundation `.env`, copied root Compose project, patched tree, manifest, allow-list, or generated skill bundle.

Four-layer resolution uses `containers.env`, Search `.env`, Search `overrides.env`, and `_builds/search-standalone/override.env` with the build `compose.yml`; normalized `resolved.yml` validates directly, selected owners and peers resolve, excluded services do not resolve, no selected profile token is unknown, no service retains a `profiles:` gate, no real `${...}` interpolation remains unresolved, no `/path/to/deploy/docker` or `<HOST_IP>` sentinel remains, and every checked-in bind source exists with the expected file/directory type.

The generated architecture conveys that both ingestion modes — streaming (RTSP) and on-demand (upload) — reach the pipeline through VIOS, and that the RT-CV, RT-Embed, and RT-VLM tagging write paths are provisioned directly (REST/service-native, no agent tier); equivalent wording satisfies this, exact phrasing is not required.
No file under `{{repo_root}}/deploy/docker/` is modified.

expects.query: Deploy the validated `_builds/search-standalone/resolved.yml` directly as the only Compose file, wait for the selected services to become ready, and leave the deployment running for runtime validation. Do not create or use helper Compose overrides such as `no-cpu-limit.yml`; if `resolved.yml` itself cannot deploy, report that blocker. Treat the generated deployment as immutable during and after deployment: do not edit files under `deploy/docker/`, do not regenerate the build, and do not patch service configs while diagnosing readiness.
checks: Deployment uses the validated `_builds/search-standalone/resolved.yml` as the only Compose file and starts it with `docker compose ... up -d`; harmless deployment options such as `-p <project>` or `--build` are allowed, but it must not re-read Foundation env files, supply `--profile`, use an invented Compose profile, or deploy a copied Compose project.

All selected long-running containers are present and not exited, restarting, or dead — **including `vss-rtvi-vlm`**; all selected one-shot containers exit 0; and excluded services (including `vss-agent`, `vss-ui`, `phoenix`, and every `llm_*`/`vlm_*` NIM) are not running. A Docker `unhealthy` label alone is not a failure when the explicit service readiness probes in this step pass.

`curl -sf http://localhost:${RTVI_CV_HOST_PORT:-9000}/ready` returns HTTP 200, RT-Embed readiness responds successfully, and RT-VLM readiness (`curl -sf http://localhost:${RTVI_VLM_PORT:-8018}/v1/health/ready`) responds successfully with a nonempty served-model list at `GET /v1/models`.

Curling the operate routes through the ingress origin (`http://localhost:${HAPROXY_HOST_PORT:-7777}`) proves the single HAProxy fronts each deployed backend, probed at the real backend paths `vss configure` uses (the mounts strip the prefix to the backend, so the bare mount reaches the backend root and 404s): `/vst/api/v1/sensor/version`, `/rtvi-embed/v1/models`, `/rtvi-vlm/v1/models`, and `/rtvi-cv/api/v1/stream/add` each answer a present status (`200`/`401`/`403`/`405`, e.g. `405` for the POST-only `/rtvi-cv/api/v1/stream/add` under a `GET`), not `404` (which `vss configure` records as absent) and not the host-allowlist reject, and `/elasticsearch` is fronted with the edge guard in force: a `GET` against `/elasticsearch/_cat/indices` routes through, while `PUT`/`DELETE` return `405` and a cluster-admin path such as `/elasticsearch/_cluster/health` returns `403` (the guard is a denylist, not read-only: top-level `POST` writes such as `/elasticsearch/_bulk` still reach ES by design); the bare origin `/` redirects (`302`) to `/kibana/` while every other unmatched path returns `404`, so an unfronted probe path such as `/api/v1/videos` returns `404` (recorded absent by `vss configure`), never a redirect to Kibana's `200`; RT-VLM is fronted at `/rtvi-vlm`, so `/rtvi-vlm/v1/models` through the origin answers a present status and `vss configure` records `rt_vlm` present (activating the fail-open search critic); the provision recipe may use loopback `${RTVI_VLM_PORT:-8018}` from the deploy host or the origin from a remote host.

expects.query: The stack built in step 1 and deployed in step 2 is running. Provision RT-CV, RT-Embed, and RT-VLM tagging by direct REST from VIOS per `vss-manage-video-io-storage` `references/provision-vios-source.md` — the tagging leg is a controlled `POST /v1/generate_captions` with a JSON-tag prompt, `response_format` `json_object`, `temperature` 0, and 5-second chunks, distinct from free-form dense captioning. Prove both upload and live RTSP paths, then record the deployment with `vss configure --base-url <build-origin>` and query the populated indexes back with `vss search run embed`, `vss search run tag`, and `vss search run fusion`, deferring query mechanics to `vss-search-archive`, and report results covering the Foundation and its delta, changed knobs, readiness across the deployed services, playback for both the upload and live paths (echoing the runtime-discovered VIOS proxy URL verbatim), Kafka end offsets before and after processing for `mdx-raw`, `mdx-embed`, `mdx-embed-filtered`, `mdx-behavior`, and `mdx-vlm-captions`, Elasticsearch evidence including the `default_<sanitized-sensorId>` tag index, and the `vss search run` round-trip results.
checks: An uploaded video remains retrievable through VIOS and produces RT-CV detection output, RT-Embed embedding output, and RT-VLM tagging output; the three legs share one VIOS `sensorId` (the shared-id rule) and the upload `creation_time` anchor is passed to every upload consumer (the upload-date rule).

A live NvStreamer synthetic RTSP source is registered through VIOS; its VIOS live-proxy URL (`rtsp://${HOST_IP}:30554/live/<sensorId>`) is discovered by reading the aggregate `/sensor/streams` or `/proxy/streams` for that `sensorId` — the per-sensor `/sensor/<sensorId>/streams` can stay empty past the brief post-add race — retried with backoff past an empty/404 first read, never constructed and never replaced by the raw NvStreamer RTSP — and RT-CV, RT-Embed, and RT-VLM tagging are driven from that discovered proxy URL.

The RT-VLM tagging leg calls `POST http://localhost:${RTVI_VLM_PORT:-8018}/v1/generate_captions` with a **controlled JSON-tag prompt** (asking for `{"tags":[...],"description":"..."}` only), `response_format={"type":"json_object"}`, `temperature=0`, `chunk_duration=5`, and `stream=false` for the VOD upload, carrying the VIOS `sensorId` as the body `id` and the VIOS storage URL as `url` with `creation_time` set to the upload anchor — NOT a free-form dense-captioning prompt — and then releases the temporary RT-VLM file asset with `DELETE /v1/files/{sensorId}`; for the live path it registers via `POST /v1/streams/add` with `id`/`sensor_name` set to the VIOS sensorId and tears down with `DELETE /v1/generate_captions/{id}` then `DELETE /v1/streams/delete/{id}`.

Kafka end offsets for `mdx-raw`, `mdx-embed`, `mdx-embed-filtered`, `mdx-behavior`, and `mdx-vlm-captions` are recorded before and after processing and all increase; the `mdx-vlm-captions` increase is the tagging leg's publish evidence.

Elasticsearch contains detection documents (`mdx-raw-*`), behavior documents (`mdx-behavior-*`), filtered-embedding documents (`mdx-embed-filtered-*`) with a populated dense_vector field, **and tag documents in a `default_<sanitized-sensorId>` index** whose `text` field parses as the controlled tag JSON (`{"tags":[...],"description":"..."}`) and whose `sensor.id.keyword` matches the resolved VIOS sensor ID, all attributable to the processed media.

A `vss search run embed` query against the deployed build — the deployment first recorded via `vss configure --base-url http://${HOST_IP}:${HAPROXY_HOST_PORT:-7777}` (re-run after ingestion so the index list is populated), with no `--deployment`/`--profile` selector and no explicit endpoint flags — returns ranked results for the ingested media from the populated `mdx-embed-filtered-*` index, and a `vss search run tag` query returns BM25-ranked results (lexical score, not cosine similarity) for a keyword drawn from the generated tags from the populated `default_<sanitized-sensorId>` index, proving both the embed and tag read paths round-trip through the single ingress.

No duplicate Kafka or Elasticsearch stack is deployed, no incident or verification index is created (no `alert-bridge`, `mdx-incidents`, or `mdx-vlm-incidents`), the agent-backed three-step workflow (`POST /api/v1/videos` + `/complete`) is NOT invoked (this is the headless path), no file under `deploy/docker/` is modified, and the final response reports the Foundation, delta, changed knobs, readiness, playback, Kafka offsets, Elasticsearch evidence including the `default_*` tag index, and the query round-trip results.
